transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-11
Start: 2027-04-11 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 mins
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: ff-20270411-74a9

Summary:
Quick partner + Redwood + Southbridge sync to hand off co-sell motions, map high-priority accounts, and align on next steps for a pilot/POC and the joint close plan. Security questions surfaced re: on-prem VPC routing and KMS; pricing sensitivity around Dedicated commit vs hosted burst. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Deal prioritization (three target accounts)
- Technical validation plan and benchmark ownership
- Security/compliance asks (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
- Joint pricing and contract cadence
- Upcoming partner-led exec intro

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miles: Okay, hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we wanted to get the partner involved and make sure we have a clean handoff. I'm Jordan, AE on this deal, joining from Redwood.
[00:14] Carlos Mendez: Hey Jordan, thanks. I'm Carlos, procurement. We'll try to keep this short. Aisha and Nora here are the technical leads.
[00:22] Aisha Khan: Hi. Quick on schedule, we have a Q3 target for production roll if things look good.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Great. I'm Priya from Solutions Eng, I'll drive the latency/cost baseline and the test harness with you, Aisha.
[00:37] Liam O'Connor: Liam (partner) — our GTM team wants clarity on the close plan and joint logo placement, also any joint exec intro helps.
[00:45] Marta Li: Marta, CSM — I'll manage onboarding artifacts and SLA expectations post-sign.
[01:03] Jordan Miles: Cool. High-level: Southbridge has three named accounts we've prioritized — the internal banking platform, a compliance-heavy trading desk, and a customer service bot modernization piece. We want to figure out which one we pilot and what partner plays support that. Priya, can you speak to the technical validation steps?
[01:20] Priya Shah: Yeah, so baseline first — small test set to measure p50/p95 latency, tokens-per-second and cost across hosted vs a Dedicated pool. We'll include a quantized variant for cost comparisons. Aisha, do you have sample prompts and typical sequence lengths?
[01:33] Aisha Khan: Yeah, most are 120–400 tokens, conversational multi-turn for service bots, the trading desk is heavier with 800+ sometimes — but that's rarer. We can share a seed set by tomorrow.
[01:44] Priya Shah: Perfect, that helps. For the trading desk cases we'll recommend the Dedicated variant with fixed KV cache sizing, otherwise for the bots the hosted plus prefix caching might be enough to hit latency SLOs.
[02:05] Nora Patel: On security: two asks. One — can you confirm we can use our KMS and key rotation policy? Two — audit logs and where they live. We need the SOC 2 attachments and an architecture diagram showing VPC peering or private link.
[02:20] Jordan Miles: Yes, we can support customer-managed KMS in the Private deployment option; for Hosted we have encryption at rest with Redwood-managed keys, but we can discuss a hybrid for the pilot. We'll send SOC 2 and the network diagram after this call.
[02:34] Carlos Mendez: Is there latency impact when we move to a VPC/private path? That's a concern for the trading desk.
[02:40] Priya Shah: Slight overhead sometimes due to routing, but with colocated regions and tuned kernels we usually see <10% delta; we'll include region-specific runs in the benchmark.
[03:00] Liam O'Connor: From the partner side, we also need to know the pricing sensitivity so we can craft our bundle. Are you expecting a long-term Dedicated commit or a shorter Reserved+burst hybrid?
[03:13] Jordan Miles: Southbridge has expressed cost sensitivity — they like the predictability of Dedicated but are worried about utilization. We're proposing a 6–12 month Reserved with autoscale burst and an opt-out clause if utilization stays below 40%.
[03:29] Marta Li: For onboarding, can we estimate ramp timelines? Dev -> UAT -> Prod with two sprints for integration? That affects pricing schedule.
[03:38] Priya Shah: Integration usually 2–4 weeks for API integration, another 2 weeks for data flows + security reviews. If we do a Dedicated warm-up we add 1–2 weeks for capacity provisioning.
[03:55] Aisha Khan: That timeline sounds okay if we get the SOC2 and architecture by early next week. Also, can you send us a sample SLA and an incident response playbook?
[04:10] Jordan Miles: Absolutely, Marta will attach the SLA template. We'll also share our incident playbook — note many of these are customizable per enterprise.
[04:22] Carlos Mendez: We had a competitor (Anthropic) pitch that they could do some parts on-prem which lowered perceived risk. How do you differentiate on the ROI side?
[04:33] Jordan Miles: Good call out — our differentiation is in predictable unit economics plus routing and fallback policies: if a Dedicated pool has issues we can route to a compatible model in another region or a lower-cost quantized variant. Also, our console gives token-level cost breakdowns so you can track exactly where costs come from.
[04:54] Liam O'Connor: Also call out that partners will run customer success bundles — that helps them feel comfortable with long-term adoption.
[05:02] Priya Shah: On the technical deep dive side, we should run a 60–90 minute bench session with their team and the trading desk sample. Priya -> that's me, I'll own the run.
[05:10] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Can we include 1) p50/p95 tokens, 2) cost per 1k tokens, 3) tail behavior for sequences >1k tokens?
[05:22] Priya Shah: Yep will include all three. We'll log KV cache hit rates too.
[05:31] Nora Patel: For compliance, two more items: audit retention timeline and where logs of query payloads live. We need to ensure no PII persists beyond configured retention.
[05:42] Jordan Miles: We honor customer-configured retention for Private deployments; for Hosted we have default retention policies that can be shortened. We'll send the detailed doc.
[05:53] Carlos Mendez: On commercial terms: is Redwood open to a co-sell revenue split model or prefer referral fees? Partner wants clarity.
[06:01] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, our GTM is flexible. Typically a % of net revenue for the first 12 months, or a discounted embed price and partner handles resell margin.
[06:10] Jordan Miles: We can do a few structures — referral, co-sell with shared discount tiers, or reseller with seat-based margins. We'll draft a few options in the joint close plan.
[06:24] Marta Li: Also want to note escalation path post-sign: SE runbooks, support SLAs, and onboarding milestones — we'll include those in the onboarding checklist.
[06:34] Carlos Mendez: Are there any integration pre-reqs on our side? E.g., firewall rules, IP allowlist, etc.
[06:41] Priya Shah: We'll provide exact IP ranges and firewall guidance. If you choose Private, you'll likely do VPC peering or private link and we'll provide templates.
[06:53] Jordan Miles: All right, let's talk priority accounts. Which of the three should be pilot? Which has highest exec sponsor and lowest compliance blockers?
[07:02] Aisha Khan: The customer service bot has the fastest path — low compliance barriers and clear success metric (average handle time reduction). The trading desk is complex and will take longer.
[07:14] Carlos Mendez: I agree; we prefer bot → trading desk. Exec sponsor is stronger on the bot side.
[07:20] Liam O'Connor: Partner can help with integration for the bot; we have an adapter they've used before.
[07:27] Jordan Miles: Good. So pilot = customer service bot. Technical validation: Priya to run baseline; timeline: sample prompts tomorrow, run bench next week. Commercial: Jordan to send joint close plan and pricing with partner contribution models by 2027-04-15. Security: Marta/Jordan to send SOC2 and architecture diagram by 2027-04-13. Exec intro: Jordan to schedule CIO intro.
[07:58] Interrupt (overlap): Unclear speaker: right — sorry go on.
[08:05] Priya Shah: One nuance: for the bot we recommend hosted with prefix KV caching and then if latency/throughput concerns appear switch to a small Dedicated pool. That gives cost savings initially.
[08:19] Aisha Khan: Does prefix caching preserve privacy? Some of our prompts include partial PII for context.
[08:27] Priya Shah: Caching respects the same retention and redaction policies; we can configure to avoid caching PII.
[08:35] Nora Patel: Good — we will need to sign off on the exact retention flags.
[08:42] Jordan Miles: On the commercial note — I want visibility into partner margins so we can model net price. Liam, can you share typical partner discount rates? It will help us propose a price bands that close.
[08:55] Liam O'Connor: Typically 10–20% depending on volume and commitment. For pilot volumes we'll push to 15%.
[09:03] Jordan Miles: Okay we'll include a band and make partner contribution explicit.
[09:10] Carlos Mendez: Any blockers on procurement side? Contract terms, ISV addendums?
[09:16] Jordan Miles: Our standard enterprise agreement plus DPA; for resale we add a partner addendum. We can send redlines earlier in the process.
[09:25] Martha Li: (laughs) Marta — I'll track contract milestones once deal goes to legal.
[09:33] Aisha Khan: On a technical nit: for the trading desk, do you support model pinning and pinned quantized weights? We've seen latency variance with quantized rollouts.
[09:45] Priya Shah: We do model pinning and recommended quantization profiles per workload; for trading desk we might avoid heavy quantization to preserve numeric stability.
[09:58] Nora Patel: And KMS integration — will our key be in HSM? We require HSM-backed keys for certain data classes.
[10:07] Jordan Miles: Yes, HSM-backed customer KMS supported in Private deployment. We'll note that in the security doc.
[10:14] Carlos Mendez: Great. Anything else on the pipeline?
[10:20] Liam O'Connor: Just one ask from partner GTM — permission to reference Southbridge in a case study contingent on pilot success. We'll include that in the joint close plan as an opt-in clause.
[10:31] Jordan Miles: Fine, add an opt-in marketing clause.
[10:36] Action recap (quick): Jordan to send joint pricing + close plan, Priya to run bench, Marta to prepare onboarding checklist and SLA, Nora to confirm compliance items, partner to share margin expectations.
[10:50] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. Can we tentatively schedule the mapping workshop for 2027-04-18 at 16:00 UTC?
[10:57] Jordan Miles: I'll propose that in the follow-up invite.
[11:02] Priya Shah: I'll book a 90-minute bench window with Aisha for next week and share a Colab + spreadsheet.
[11:10] Aisha Khan: Thanks. Expect seed prompts by end of day tomorrow.
[11:15] Jordan Miles: Cool. Any last questions?
[11:20] Nora Patel: One small ask — include a short table in the security doc mapping controls to our internal policy identifiers. That speeds review.
[11:29] Jordan Miles: Will do.
[11:33] Carlos Mendez: Alright thanks everyone. Jordan, we'll wait for the docs and the invite.
[11:39] Jordan Miles: Thanks all. Wrap up — follow-ups in notes and I'll send the joint close plan by Friday.
[11:45] Meeting end.
